author: haiku
label: seeded-01-01
changes: Added a short 'Words used' section defining primary, replica, job, queue, export record, multipart upload, exports bucket, and filters and columns, for a reader new to the stack.
Rewrote each step to state what starts it, what data moves, where state is kept, and what happens on failure, as the brief asks. The draft gave one line per step.

Added that the filters and columns are copied onto the export record, because the job runs later and the page URL is gone. The job payload holds only the export id, which keeps it under the 64 KB limit.
Added the replica-only rule and the 60-second request limit to the small-report path.
Added the unique index for one active export per user and report, and how a race between two clicks is handled.
Added the gap between inserting the row and enqueueing the job, and what happens if the process dies between them.
Added the job's batch-and-part memory bounds and the part-count check against the 2-million-row report.
Added handling for at-least-once delivery: the job stops on repeat runs, and an `email_sent_at` field lets a retry send only the missing email.
Set the order in the final-failure handler so the row is marked failed before the email is sent.
Added a fresh-link download endpoint, because the emailed link expires after 24 hours while the file lasts 7 days.
Added the step for a file that has expired after 7 days, and noted the missing existence check in the storage helpers.
Added open questions for the 30-minute time limit, partial small files, rebuild consistency, stuck queued rows, bearer links, changed filters, and the unfiltered row count.
Defined the terms a reader new to the stack needs: endpoint, keyset paging, unique index, payload, signed link, and at-least-once delivery.
Explained the queue's retry, timeout and memory limits in plain terms, including that no progress is kept between attempts.
Replaced the 'go to step 3 / step 4' wording in step 2 with what each branch does.
Spelled out in step 5 what a 'repeat run' is and why a done row with no email_sent_at still needs step 7.
Described the step 5 upload loop more plainly: the buffer is uploaded as a part when it reaches 5 MB, and etags are kept in order for completion.
Clarified in step 6 why the status is saved before the email, and what the page shows if the email fails.
Clarified in step 8 the two ways the expired-file case can be handled.
Clarified the open questions in shorter sentences without changing their options. No content was removed or added beyond these clarifications.
Added a short "How the pieces fit" section before the glossary so a reader sees the page, the button, the job, storage and the status table in one view.
Defined terms the first draft used without explanation: row ID, attempt, ETag, template, bucket, and what "at least once" means in practice.
Replaced the jargon-heavy definition of at-least-once delivery with the plain consequence: every step must be safe to repeat.
Spelled out HTTP status codes (403 forbidden, 200, 202 accepted) and stated that the permission check runs before any data is read.
In step 3, said plainly that bytes are sent as they are produced and not held until the end.
In step 5, made the buffer loop explicit with a bulleted sub-list and stated that the final part may be smaller than 5 MB.
In step 5, said that the ETags are passed in part order, since the join step needs them in that order.
Added a clause that the 10 MB memory figure is the most held at once, so the bound is easy to check.
Kept every step, number, limit, open question and the document's format unchanged in substance.
